Condensed Matter Theory

How light, spins and the lattice exchange energy and angular momentum

I am a theoretical physicist working on ultrafast magnetism, magnon–phonon coupling, chiral phonons and topological transport in magnetic and quantum materials. I link first-principles calculations to large-scale simulations that I develop myself, and work closely with experimental groups.

Research

My research asks how we can use light, symmetry and the lattice to control magnetic order: how energy and angular momentum flow between electrons, spins and phonons, which quasiparticles carry them, and how these pathways can be engineered in magnetic and quantum materials.

Spin–lattice coupling and ultrafast dynamics

Angular-momentum transfer between spins and lattice from first principles, non-thermal magnons in ultrafast demagnetization, femtosecond switching of antiferromagnets, and energy flow in laser-excited heterostructures.

Chiral phonons and magnon–phonon hybrids

How magnetism gives phonons a twist: chirality-selective magnon–phonon coupling, phonons carrying angular momentum, and their signatures in anomalous transport, including in altermagnets.

Topology and transport in quantum materials

Floquet and phonon-driven engineering of topological magnons in 2D van der Waals magnets, magnonic spin and orbital Nernst effects, and the stochastic dynamics of skyrmions.

Modeling complex magnetic heterostructures

Multiscale simulations of complex magnetic structures including non-collinear magnets, altermagnets, ferrimagnets, and multilayer heterostructures.

Methods

First-principles calculations (Quantum ESPRESSO, VASP, ELK, Abinit) · spin–lattice Langevin dynamics · quantum Boltzmann equations · linear response and Green's functions · Floquet theory · GPU-accelerated HPC codes (C/C++, Fortran, CUDA, MPI, OpenMP)
